name: reference-heavy-mkdocs-site
query: Review this MkDocs documentation for a developer-facing GitHub Action. The nav has Home, Actions Reference, Schemas, and Contributing. Give me the highest-impact improvements.
expected_behavior: Inspects the actual landing/reference content before assuming pages are missing
Evaluates first-success, common-task, reference, and troubleshooting journeys
Identifies task-oriented guidance as a likely gap when evidence supports it
Suggests a compact revised navigation rather than creating taxonomy for its own sake
Prioritizes findings by developer impact

name: documentation-code-drift
query: Review the docs and action.yml. The docs say input 'mode' defaults to deploy, but action.yml defaults it to template.
expected_behavior: Treats action.yml as a source of truth for the Action input
Reports the mismatch as a high or critical correctness issue depending on impact
Explains the user impact and names the exact smallest fix
Checks for the stale default in examples and other reference pages

name: good-small-project
query: Review a small MkDocs project whose index page contains a complete quickstart, actions.md is exhaustive and generated from metadata, schemas.md is source-derived, and troubleshooting is a section on index.md because there are only three common errors.
expected_behavior: Does not insist on separate pages merely to match a framework
Rewards concise information architecture that serves the reader journeys
Focuses on actual correctness, findability, and maintenance evidence
Avoids low-value style nitpicking

name: mkdocs-build-quality-gate
query: Review mkdocs.yml and docs CI. Several internal links are stale, a nav entry points to a renamed file, and CI runs mkdocs build without strict mode.
expected_behavior: Identifies the broken navigation and links as concrete defects
Recommends using the project-compatible strict/link validation mechanism
Does not install or upgrade dependencies during a review without permission
Separates current breakage from longer-term toolchain maintenance recommendations

name: how-to-missing-verification
query: Review docs/guides/deploy.md. It is a how-to with prerequisites and three exact deployment commands, but after the final state-changing command the page ends with links to other docs. There is a supported status command in the repository that would confirm the deployment succeeded.
expected_behavior: Recognizes the page as a task-oriented how-to and applies a how-to-specific contract
Flags the missing verification step because success is not self-evident and a supported check exists
Recommends the verified repository status command rather than inventing a check
Does not demand unrelated tutorial, concept, FAQ, or decorative sections

name: unsupported-material-syntax
query: Review an MkDocs Material site where docs/setup.md uses ???+ collapsible questions, === content tabs, and a mermaid fence. mkdocs.yml enables admonition and superfences, but not pymdownx.details, pymdownx.tabbed, or a Mermaid custom fence/plugin.
expected_behavior: Maps each sampled non-standard construct to the extension or configuration it requires
Reports the unsupported details, tabs, and Mermaid rendering as functional documentation defects
Does not assume Material syntax is enabled merely because the theme is Material
Suggests either enabling the required project-compatible extensions or simplifying the authored Markdown

name: material-visual-overuse-and-house-style
query: Review a valid MkDocs Material guide that wraps routine paragraphs in admonitions, puts sequential steps into tabs, and uses a Mermaid diagram for a simple A-to-B relationship. The repository style guide also requires 100-character lines and relative internal links.
expected_behavior: Flags tabs/admonitions/diagram only where they reduce clarity or hide the task flow, rather than treating Material features as inherently good or bad
Recommends simpler prose or ordered steps when the visual feature adds no comprehension value
Enforces the repository's explicit line-length and link-style rules as project conventions
Does not generalize those house-style rules into universal documentation criteria
